title: Air Canada Flight 143 / Gimli Glider: metric fuel calculation as survivable numeric-representation failure
summary: Air Canada Flight 143 is encoded as a positive-control case for MKH-PAT-0001: a unit/representation boundary mattered materially, but the outcome was survivable because of flight-crew recovery. It is not encoded as a simple “metric error” anecdote; the official report ties the event to inoperative gauges, abnormal drip-stick fueling, wrong conversion factor, mixed fleet context, responsibility ambiguity, training, manuals, and organizational deficiencies.

status_history.note: Added as first explicit positive-control record for numeric-representation pattern calibration.

place.location: Gimli, Manitoba, Canada; diversion from Air Canada Flight 143 route after fuel exhaustion over Red Lake, Ontario

claims.claim: The Air Canada Boeing 767 made an emergency landing at Gimli on July 23, 1983 after running out of fuel; the report states that the aircraft left Montreal and Ottawa with inoperative fuel gauges and insufficient fuel, and that there was no loss of life or significant physical injuries.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: The official report identifies the abnormal-fueling conversion pathway: drip-stick readings were converted through a 1.77 pounds-per-litre factor, while the metric 767 required kilograms; the same incorrect conversion was used at both Montreal and Ottawa, leaving about half the fuel the crew believed was aboard.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: The report treats the event as systemic rather than a single arithmetic mistake, including a mixed metric/non-metric fleet, unclear responsibility, inadequate training/communication/manuals, lack of cross-check/double-check procedures, and corporate/organizational deficiencies.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction or narrows its scope.

claims.claim: For the cube, Air Canada Flight 143 is a positive-control case for MKH-PAT-0001: it shares the numeric representation / unit-boundary mechanism, while its survivable recovery prevents the pattern from being calibrated only on catastrophic losses.
what_would_change_status: A later second-pass review finds the unit-conversion causal role overstated, or a better control taxonomy separates aviation fuel-loading workflow from software/interface numeric-representation failures.

evidence_refs.support_type: positive-control relationship to numeric representation pattern

limitations: Record is a pattern-control case, not a full aviation accident monograph.
Does not encode individual blame or disciplinary outcomes beyond source-supported system factors.

type_payload.system: Air Canada Boeing 767 fuel-quantity / abnormal fueling / flight-management workflow
sequence_of_events: Fuel gauges inoperative; abnormal fueling required drip-stick/manual calculations.
Ground and flight personnel used a 1.77 pounds-per-litre factor in a metric kilograms fuel workflow.
Aircraft departed with insufficient fuel; fuel exhaustion occurred in flight.
Crew diverted and landed at Gimli with no loss of life or significant physical injuries.
type_payload.proximate_cause: fuel exhaustion after insufficient fuel was loaded under an abnormal manual-fuel-calculation workflow
contributing_factors: wrong conversion factor for litres-to-kilograms path
inoperative fuel gauges and maintenance/dispatch ambiguity
latent_conditions: organization-wide metric transition not fully supported at operational interfaces
manual abnormal procedure did not provide robust independent verification
knowledge of pounds-vs-kilograms boundary did not land as a hard control

pattern_control_role.why: Official source-backed unit/representation boundary materially causal; not one of the original three support cases used to promote the pattern.
pattern_control_role.why_not_mature_by_itself: Still does not provide a negative control or caught-before-harm counterexample.

not_this: not a simple metric-system joke or single-person arithmetic anecdote
not a claim that all unit-conversion incidents share the same organizational pathway
not a claim that survivable outcome means low severity

handling_notes: Avoid “pilot error” reduction; preserve official report’s systemic/organizational framing.
Do not romanticize the near-catastrophe as entertainment; encode survivability as pattern-calibration evidence.

unknowns: No second-pass full PDF extraction or local hash yet.
Regulatory/practice changes after the report are not yet separately encoded.
Need a negative-control case where numeric representation is present but not explanatory.
